newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee exports seen up by 1 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee exports seen up by 1 mln bags.

text.p: Colombia's coffee exports should total about 11.6 million 60-kg bags in 1997, up from 10.6 million in 1996, National Bankers' Association (ANIF) said Thursday.
The forecast, which coincides with previous estimates by National Coffee Growers' Federation, was reiterated by ANIF despite unusually heavy rains during last month's flowering period.
Some private exporters have said the rains were likely to cut total production during the 1996-97 coffee year to no more than 10 million 60-kg bags.

ANIF did not specify what its export forecast was based on. But it said world coffee prices were seen holding at an average of $1.35 per pound in 1997 and that Colombia's coffee income was expected to total $1.9 billion, up from $1.7 billion in 1996.

Gilberto Arango Londono, a former head of National Coffee Exporters' Association, added his voice, meanwhile, to a growing chorus of calls for an urgent hike in Colombia's internal coffee price to bring it closer into line with international prices.
Arango, who said the 12 percent increase in the internal price announced on Jan 31 fell far short of growers' expectations, spoke in an interview with the RCN radio network.

Low internal prices have led a growing number of producers to smuggle their coffee across Colombia's southern border with Ecuador, where it can be sold on the free market at substantially higher prices than the going rate in Colombia, he said.
Agriculture Minister Cecilia Lopez hinted Wednesday that the government was considering a moderate increase in the internal price, currently set at 248,125 pesos per 125-kg load.
